title: Number of Ways to Buy Pens and Pencils
summary: Given an amount of money, and the costs of a pen and a pencil, determine the number of unique combinations of pens and pencils that can be purchased with the given budget.
statement: Given an amount of money, and the costs of a pen and a pencil, determine the number of unique combinations of pens and pencils that can be purchased with the given budget.
constraints: Choose nonnegative integer quantities of both item types.
A combination is valid when its total cost is at most the budget, so money may remain.
Different quantity pairs count separately, including buying zero of either or both.
hints: Fix the number of the first item, then count all affordable quantities of the second.
For first from zero through total//cost1, the second quantity has floor(remaining/cost2)+1 choices.
Sum (total-first*cost1)//cost2+1 across every feasible first quantity.
Every valid quantity pair has one unique first quantity and is counted once among that iteration’s complete range of second quantities.
editorial: Every valid quantity pair has one unique first quantity and is counted once among that iteration’s complete range of second quantities.

tests.explanation: For zero, one, or two pens there are five, three, or one pencil choices, totaling nine.
Only buying zero of both items fits, so the answer is one.
